questions.q: On which date in 1789 was the Bastille fortress-prison stormed in Paris?
questions.explanation: The Bastille was stormed on 14 July 1789, a key event of the French Revolution.

questions.q: Who became the first king of unified Italy in 1861?
questions.explanation: Victor Emmanuel II, the ruler of Sardinia-Piedmont, was proclaimed king of the unified Italy.

questions.q: Who was Count Cavour?
options: The chief minister of Sardinia-Piedmont who led the movement to unify the Italian states
The leader of the Red Shirts
questions.explanation: Cavour was a statesman, not a revolutionary, who used diplomacy and an alliance with France to unify Italy.

questions.q: In economic matters, liberal nationalism stood for
options: freedom of markets and the abolition of state-imposed restrictions on the movement of goods and capital
questions.explanation: Middle-class liberals wanted free markets, and this was one reason for the Zollverein.

questions.q: Why did weavers in Silesia revolt in 1845?
options: They wanted to join the Prussian army
They disliked the use of cotton
Contractors who supplied raw material paid them very low rates for finished cloth
They wanted the Pope to rule them
questions.explanation: Weavers protested against contractors who reduced their payments, which shows the economic hardship that fed the unrest of the 1840s.

questions.q: How did the Romantic movement contribute to the growth of nationalism?
options: By emphasising folk culture, language and history to create a sense of shared heritage
questions.explanation: Romantics such as Herder stressed the importance of folk songs, dances and the national language.

questions.q: What was the aim of the Congress of Vienna of 1815?
questions.answer: The European powers met after Napoleon’s defeat to undo most of the changes he had brought and restore the monarchies he had overthrown. They also set up new boundaries, such as restoring the Bourbon dynasty in France, to keep a balance of power in Europe.
keyPoints: Create a new balance of power in Europe
questions.explanation: The settlement reflected the conservative aims of the victors.

questions.q: Why did the Polish language become a symbol of national resistance in the 19th century?
questions.answer: Poland had been divided among Russia, Prussia and Austria. After a failed uprising in 1831, Russia tried to impose its own language. The Poles used the Polish language in church and religious teaching, and priests who refused to use Russian were punished, so language became a symbol of resistance.
keyPoints: Poland was partitioned among three powers
Polish used in church as an act of resistance
questions.explanation: Language preserved national identity under foreign rule.

questions.q: Bengal was partitioned in 1905 by the Viceroy
questions.explanation: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905, which led to the Swadeshi Movement.

questions.q: Who wrote the song Vande Mataram?
questions.explanation: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote Vande Mataram in the 1870s; it became a popular song of the national movement.

questions.q: In 1921 a tricolour Swaraj flag with a spinning wheel in the centre was designed by
questions.explanation: Gandhiji designed the flag; the spinning wheel symbolised self-help.

questions.q: Which movement from 1905 encouraged boycott of foreign goods and the use of Indian-made goods?
questions.explanation: The Swadeshi Movement began in Bengal in response to the partition and promoted Indian goods.

questions.q: Why did the First World War increase discontent in India?
options: It caused heavy taxes, forced recruitment, and rising prices and shortages
It led to the immediate end of British rule
questions.explanation: Indians were burdened by war expenses, recruitment and inflation, which fuelled anger against colonial rule.

questions.q: Why were rich peasant communities such as the Patidars of Gujarat active in the Civil Disobedience Movement?
options: Falling prices made it hard to pay the fixed revenue demand, so they wanted it reduced
They were forced to join by landlords
They wanted to give up farming
questions.explanation: During the trade depression, prices of cash crops fell but the revenue demand remained, so they supported the movement.

questions.q: Describe the Jallianwala Bagh incident of 13 April 1919.
questions.answer: On the day of Baisakhi, a crowd gathered at Jallianwala Bagh in Amritsar, many to protest against the Rowlatt Act. General Dyer ordered troops to fire on the unarmed crowd in an enclosed space, killing and wounding hundreds. It caused widespread anger across India.
keyPoints: General Dyer ordered firing on unarmed people
questions.explanation: The massacre turned many Indians against British rule.

questions.q: Why did many Dalits not take part in the Civil Disobedience Movement with enthusiasm?
questions.answer: The Congress had ignored the Dalits for a long time for fear of offending conservative high-caste groups. Dalits felt that political freedom alone would not end social discrimination, so some leaders demanded separate electorates and their own organisations.
keyPoints: Political freedom alone would not end social discrimination
questions.explanation: Dalits wanted their social problems addressed alongside political demands.

questions.topic: The Making of a Global World
questions.q: The Silk Routes were so named because
options: they were built by silk merchants of Venice
Chinese silk was a major item carried along them
questions.explanation: Chinese silk travelled along these routes to Europe, Central Asia and elsewhere.

questions.topic: The Making of a Global World
questions.q: The Bretton Woods conference of 1944 was held in the US state of
questions.explanation: The conference was held at Bretton Woods, New Hampshire.

questions.topic: The Making of a Global World
questions.q: Chutney music of Trinidad and Guyana is an example of
options: cultural blending among descendants of indentured Indian workers
questions.explanation: Indian indentured labourers and their descendants blended their traditions with local ones.

questions.topic: The Making of a Global World
questions.q: During the Great Depression, Indian peasants suffered because
options: farm prices fell sharply while the revenue demand of the government stayed high
questions.explanation: Prices of agricultural goods fell much more than the fixed revenue demand.

questions.topic: The Making of a Global World
questions.q: Why did US banks recalling their loans in the late 1920s worsen Europe’s economic crisis?
options: European countries had depended on American loans, and when recalled, many banks and firms failed
It had no effect on Europe
questions.explanation: Europe had relied heavily on American credit, so the loss of it caused bank failures and falling production.

questions.topic: The Making of a Global World
questions.q: Why did the Bretton Woods system use fixed exchange rates?
options: To bring stability to currencies and encourage trade by avoiding sharp changes
questions.explanation: Fixed, adjustable rates were meant to avoid the instability that had hurt world trade between the wars.

questions.topic: The Making of a Global World
questions.q: Who were indentured labourers, and why did many Indians become indentured workers?
questions.answer: They were workers bound by a contract to work for an employer, usually on plantations abroad, for several years to repay the cost of their passage. Many Indians, hit by poverty, debt and the decline of cottage industries, accepted such work, often misled about the conditions.
keyPoints: Bound by contract to an employer for years
Poverty and debt drove many Indians to accept the work
questions.explanation: Indentured labour was a harsh form of migration.

questions.topic: The Making of a Global World
questions.q: How did the Silk Routes help spread ideas as well as goods?
questions.answer: Merchants, travellers and preachers moved along the routes, so Buddhism spread from India through Central Asia to China, and Christian and Muslim missionaries also travelled them. Goods such as silk, textiles and spices were exchanged, and so were customs and knowledge.
keyPoints: Spread of religions such as Buddhism
questions.explanation: Trade routes were also routes of cultural exchange.

questions.topic: Industrialisation and the Age of Industry
questions.q: Richard Arkwright is known for creating
questions.explanation: Arkwright set up the cotton mill with water-powered machinery, which brought spinning under one roof.

questions.topic: Industrialisation and the Age of Industry
questions.q: Which two cities emerged as major ports and trading centres in India as old ports like Surat declined?
questions.explanation: Surat and Hooghly declined while Bombay and Calcutta grew under colonial trade.

questions.topic: Industrialisation and the Age of Industry
questions.q: Which invention allowed weavers to throw the shuttle using ropes and pulleys, making weaving faster?
questions.explanation: The fly shuttle sped up weaving and was adopted by many Indian handloom weavers.

questions.topic: Industrialisation and the Age of Industry
questions.q: How did the Swadeshi Movement affect Indian industry?
options: It reduced the demand for cloth
It raised imports of British cloth
It encouraged the use of Indian-made goods, boosting handloom and mill production
questions.explanation: The boycott of foreign cloth increased demand for Indian-made cloth.

questions.topic: Industrialisation and the Age of Industry
questions.q: Why did many British industrialists not adopt steam engines quickly in all industries?
options: The engines were costly to buy and maintain, and labour was cheap and easily available
questions.explanation: Where labour was cheap, employers saw little advantage in investing in costly machines.

questions.topic: Industrialisation and the Age of Industry
questions.q: Why did manufacturers in India use pictures of Hindu gods and goddesses on labels and calendars?
options: To appeal to buyers’ sentiments and make the product appear trustworthy and acceptable
questions.explanation: Religious images helped sell products to people who respected them.

questions.topic: Industrialisation and the Age of Industry
questions.q: What role did the railways play in industrialisation?
questions.answer: Railways moved raw materials, coal and finished goods quickly and cheaply, linked factories to markets and ports, and created demand for iron and steel, which helped other industries grow.
keyPoints: Cheaper and faster transport of goods
Created demand for iron and coal
questions.explanation: Transport is essential to industrial growth.

questions.topic: Industrialisation and the Age of Industry
questions.q: How did Indian manufacturers use advertisements to link their products with the national movement?
questions.answer: Advertisements and calendars carried messages asking people to buy goods made in India if they cared for the nation. During the Swadeshi movement, such appeals increased the sale of Indian goods and linked consumption with patriotism.
questions.explanation: Advertising helped connect industry with nationalism.

questions.topic: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.q: The first printing press in India was brought to which place by Portuguese missionaries?
questions.explanation: Portuguese missionaries brought the printing press to Goa in the sixteenth century.

questions.topic: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.q: Martin Luther was associated with the
questions.explanation: Martin Luther started the Protestant Reformation by criticising the Roman Catholic Church.

questions.topic: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.q: The Marathi newspaper Kesari was associated with
questions.explanation: Bal Gangadhar Tilak edited Kesari and used it to spread nationalist ideas.

questions.topic: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.q: Why were books expensive before the invention of printing in Europe?
options: They were copied by hand, which was slow, costly and tiring
questions.explanation: Handwritten manuscripts took months to copy, so books were rare and costly.

questions.topic: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.q: How did lending libraries and cheaper books in nineteenth-century Europe widen the reading public?
options: They made books harder to find
They were open only to nobles
They allowed working people and women, who could not afford books, to read
questions.explanation: Lending libraries gave access to books for people who could not buy them.

questions.topic: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.q: Why is Rassundari Debi’s Amar Jiban (1876) historically significant?
options: It was a map of Bengal
It was a full-length autobiography in Bengali by a woman, telling how she learnt to read in secret
questions.explanation: It gives a rare picture of a woman’s life and the obstacles to women’s education.

questions.topic: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.q: What measures did the colonial government take to control the press in India in the nineteenth century?
questions.answer: After 1857 the attitude to the press became harsher. The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 gave the government the right to censor reports and editorials in Indian-language papers; if a report was found seditious, the paper was warned, and its press could be seized.
questions.explanation: The government wished to curb nationalist writing.

questions.topic: Print Culture and the Modern World
questions.q: How did print culture create conditions for the French Revolution?
questions.answer: Print spread the ideas of Enlightenment thinkers, who attacked tradition and superstition and stressed reason. Books, pamphlets and cartoons encouraged debate and criticism of the monarchy and the Church and gave people new ways of thinking.
questions.explanation: Print created a public ready to challenge old authority.

questions.q: Resources that exist in a region but have not yet been used are called
questions.explanation: For example, the wind energy potential of Rajasthan and Gujarat has not been fully developed.

questions.q: Terrace farming is mainly practised in
questions.explanation: Steps cut into hill slopes reduce run-off and soil erosion.

questions.q: Which soil is formed from the weathering of lava rock in the Deccan Trap region?
questions.explanation: Black soil is formed from volcanic rock in the Deccan plateau.

questions.q: Which feature is typical of arid soil?
options: Strongly acidic with dense forest cover
Sandy and often saline with little humus
questions.explanation: In dry regions evaporation is high, so the soil is sandy, salty and low in humus.

questions.q: Why does deforestation lead to soil erosion?
options: Tree roots bind the soil and leaves break the force of rain, so without them soil is washed or blown away
Forests increase the speed of wind
Soil is erodible only in forests
questions.explanation: Vegetation cover protects topsoil from wind and water.

questions.q: Why is the protection of forests regarded as a form of resource conservation?
options: Forests hold soil and water and support wildlife, so destroying them harms many other resources
Cutting forests always increases soil fertility
questions.explanation: Forests are linked with soil, water, climate and biodiversity.

questions.q: What is the Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ)?
questions.answer: The EEZ extends up to 200 nautical miles from a country’s coast. Within it the country has the right to use and manage the resources of the sea, while beyond it the open ocean belongs to no one nation.
keyPoints: Extends 200 nautical miles from the coast
Country can use resources in it
questions.explanation: The EEZ gives coastal countries rights over marine resources.

questions.q: State two causes of land degradation in India, giving an example of a region for each.
questions.answer: Mining causes degradation in Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha, where deforestation leaves land scarred. Over-irrigation in Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh causes waterlogging and salinity, and overgrazing affects Gujarat and Rajasthan.
keyPoints: Mining and deforestation: Jharkhand, Odisha etc.
questions.explanation: Human activities, not only nature, degrade land.

questions.q: Which of these is a zaid (summer season) crop?
questions.explanation: Watermelon, muskmelon and cucumber are grown in the short summer season between rabi and kharif.

questions.q: Darjeeling in West Bengal is famous for
questions.explanation: Darjeeling is a well-known tea-growing region.

questions.q: Wheat grows best in conditions of
options: a cool growing season and bright warm sunshine at ripening
questions.explanation: Wheat is a rabi crop that needs cool weather to grow and warm sunshine to ripen.

questions.q: The Bhakra Nangal multipurpose project is built on the river
questions.explanation: Bhakra Nangal is on the Sutlej; Hirakud is on the Mahanadi.

questions.q: Why did Rajasthan develop traditional rainwater harvesting structures such as tankas?
options: It has heavy rain all year
It receives low and scarce rainfall, so storing rain for drinking was essential
questions.explanation: In dry regions, people stored rain in underground tanks for use through the year.

questions.q: The Narmada Bachao Andolan opposed the Sardar Sarovar dam chiefly on grounds of
options: lack of water in the reservoir
displacement of people and effects on the environment
questions.explanation: The movement raised concern over the rehabilitation of displaced villagers and environmental impacts.

questions.q: What is meant by intensive subsistence farming?
questions.answer: It is farming on small plots using simple tools and family labour, with more crops a year, practised in areas with high population pressure on land. Farmers grow mainly for their own family’s needs.
keyPoints: Small plots, simple tools, family labour
High pressure of population on land
questions.explanation: Land is scarce, so farmers try to get the most from every plot.

questions.q: Describe two technological and two institutional measures to improve Indian agriculture.
questions.answer: Technological: high-yielding seeds, fertilisers and better irrigation. Institutional: land reforms, such as abolishing intermediaries and consolidating holdings, and support measures such as minimum support prices and credit facilities for farmers.
questions.explanation: Both technology and institutions matter for agricultural growth.

questions.q: Copper is mainly used in
questions.explanation: Copper is a good conductor of electricity, so it is widely used in electrical industries.

questions.q: Tarapur in Maharashtra is known for its
questions.explanation: Tarapur has one of India’s first nuclear power stations.

questions.q: Which type of coal has the highest carbon content and is the best quality?
questions.explanation: Anthracite is the highest-grade coal, with over 80 per cent carbon.

questions.q: Mumbai High, an important oil-producing area, lies in the
options: Indian Ocean far south of India
questions.explanation: Mumbai High is an offshore oil field in the Arabian Sea off Mumbai.

questions.q: Why does India need to develop renewable sources of energy?
options: Fossil fuels are limited, much oil is imported, and they cause pollution
India has no sunlight or wind
questions.explanation: Renewable energy lowers dependence on imports and reduces pollution.

questions.q: Why are jute mills concentrated in the Hooghly basin?
options: Jute is grown nearby and cheap water transport, rail links and labour are available
questions.explanation: Raw jute, water for processing, transport and cheap labour favoured this region.

questions.q: Distinguish between ferrous and non-ferrous minerals with examples.
questions.answer: Ferrous minerals contain iron, such as iron ore, manganese and nickel. Non-ferrous minerals do not contain iron as a main element, such as copper, lead, zinc and bauxite.
keyPoints: Ferrous: contain iron, e.g. iron ore, manganese
Non-ferrous: no iron, e.g. copper, bauxite
questions.explanation: The classification depends on whether iron is a main component.

questions.q: Why is manufacturing called the backbone of economic development?
questions.answer: Manufacturing makes goods from raw materials, adds value and creates jobs, which reduces dependence on agriculture. Manufactured exports bring foreign exchange and industrial growth raises income and living standards.
questions.explanation: Manufacturing supports growth and reduces poverty.

questions.q: The head of a municipal corporation is called the
questions.explanation: A municipal corporation is headed by a Mayor, while a municipality is headed by a chairperson.

questions.q: The elected council of a village in India is called the
questions.explanation: The Gram Panchayat is the elected body at the village level.

questions.q: Which of these is an example of a federation formed by independent states coming together?
questions.explanation: In coming-together federations such as the USA, Switzerland and Australia, independent states unite to form a larger unit.

questions.q: Which is an example of power sharing among social groups?
options: Dividing power between legislature and judiciary
Reservation of seats in legislatures for socially weaker sections
Division of power between Centre and states
questions.explanation: Reserved constituencies give weaker sections a share in political power.

questions.q: Why should the powers of the Union and the states in a federation be guaranteed by the constitution?
options: So that the Union can change them at will
So that states can leave when they want
So that neither level can unilaterally change the arrangement, protecting each one’s autonomy
questions.explanation: A written, protected division of powers keeps the federal balance stable.

questions.q: How did the creation of linguistic states help national unity in India?
options: It divided the country on all matters
It ended the need for a constitution
It increased the powers of the army
Recognising people’s language identity reduced demands for separation and made them feel included
questions.explanation: Accommodating linguistic aspirations strengthened rather than weakened the country.

questions.q: Name the three levels of Panchayati Raj institutions from the village upwards.
questions.answer: The Gram Panchayat at the village level, the Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and the Zila Parishad at the district level.
questions.explanation: Together they form the rural local government.

questions.q: Compare the approaches to power sharing in Belgium and Sri Lanka.
questions.answer: Belgium accommodated its language communities by sharing power, giving equal representation in the central government and creating community governments. In Sri Lanka the Sinhala majority imposed its language and preferred its own community, which alienated Tamils and led to conflict.
questions.explanation: Accommodation reduces conflict; majoritarianism increases it.

questions.q: India is described in the Preamble as a
questions.explanation: The Preamble describes India as a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic republic.

questions.q: Parties that lose an election and keep a check on the government play the role of
questions.explanation: The opposition criticises the government and seeks to expose its failures.

questions.q: Which of these countries is usually described as having a two-party system?
questions.explanation: In the USA, power is mainly contested by the Democratic and Republican parties.

questions.q: Women’s movements in many countries have demanded
options: equal rights in politics, education and work
questions.explanation: Women’s movements campaigned for the vote, education and equal pay.

questions.q: Decisions in a democracy often take time. Why is this generally considered acceptable?
options: Consultation and debate lead to better and more acceptable decisions
Time does not matter in government
Citizens do not care about decisions
questions.explanation: Discussion allows many views to be heard, so decisions are more likely to be accepted.

questions.q: How has the mobilisation of caste groups in politics sometimes helped disadvantaged communities?
options: It has had no effect on anyone
It has pushed parties to pay attention to the concerns of disadvantaged communities, giving them a voice
questions.explanation: When groups organise, parties must take their concerns into account.

questions.q: State two merits of a multi-party system.
questions.answer: It gives voters a wider choice and allows different interests and regions to be represented in the government and legislature. Competition among parties also makes governments more responsive.
questions.explanation: Many parties reflect the diversity of a large country.

questions.q: Why is communalism considered a challenge to democracy, and what is the response of India’s Constitution?
questions.answer: Communalism uses religion as the basis of political identity and can lead to hatred and violence between communities. The Constitution makes India a secular state with no official religion, giving equal freedom of religion to all citizens.
keyPoints: Religion used as basis of politics
India is a secular state with equal rights
questions.explanation: Secularism protects both unity and individual freedom.

questions.topic: Development and the Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: The infant mortality rate shows the number of children who die before the age of one year per
questions.explanation: IMR is expressed as deaths per 1,000 live births.

questions.topic: Development and the Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: The literacy rate shows
options: the number of schools in a state
the number of teachers in a state
the proportion of people above seven years who can read and write
questions.explanation: The literacy rate is the share of the population above seven years who are literate.

questions.topic: Development and the Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: The Human Development Index combines
options: life expectancy, education and per capita income
questions.explanation: HDI uses indicators of health, education and income.

questions.topic: Development and the Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: Which of the following is a public sector undertaking?
questions.explanation: Indian Railways is owned and run by the government.

questions.topic: Development and the Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: Why do workers in the unorganised sector need protection?
options: They enjoy high wages and security
They are all owners of factories
They often have low pay, no job security and may be exploited
questions.explanation: Without regulation, these workers face irregular income and poor working conditions.

questions.topic: Development and the Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: Why does the government fix a Minimum Support Price (MSP) for some crops?
options: To make food costlier for everyone
To make sure farmers get a minimum price and are protected from sharp price falls
questions.explanation: MSP gives farmers assurance of a base price.

questions.topic: Development and the Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: Why do different people have different development goals?
questions.answer: People’s life situations differ, so their aspirations differ. A landless labourer may want regular work and fair wages, a prosperous farmer may want a good price, and a girl may want freedom and equal opportunity. What is development for one may not be for another.
questions.explanation: Development goals depend on one’s circumstances.

questions.topic: Development and the Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: Suggest two ways to increase employment in rural areas.
questions.answer: Irrigation and other farm facilities can increase work and yields. Rural infrastructure and public works such as MGNREGA, small and cottage industries, and bank credit for rural enterprises can also create jobs.
questions.explanation: Rural jobs need investment in both farming and non-farm activities.

questions.topic: Money, Credit, Globalisation and Consumer Rights
questions.q: A written order to a bank to pay a certain sum from one’s account to a named person is called a
questions.explanation: A cheque instructs the bank to pay the stated amount.

questions.topic: Money, Credit, Globalisation and Consumer Rights
questions.q: Which of these is a source of informal credit?
questions.explanation: Moneylenders, relatives and traders are informal lenders not supervised by the RBI.

questions.topic: Money, Credit, Globalisation and Consumer Rights
questions.q: Banks earn profit mainly because they
options: pay higher interest on deposits than they charge on loans
charge higher interest on loans than they pay on deposits
questions.explanation: The difference between interest charged on loans and interest paid on deposits is the bank’s income.

questions.topic: Money, Credit, Globalisation and Consumer Rights
questions.q: A multinational company is one that
options: owns or controls production in more than one country
questions.explanation: MNCs have production units or offices in several countries.

questions.topic: Money, Credit, Globalisation and Consumer Rights
questions.q: Why is the right to information important for consumers?
options: It protects them from unfair trade practices and helps them make wise choices
It forces them to buy more
questions.explanation: Knowing the quality, quantity, price and ingredients of goods helps consumers avoid being cheated.

questions.topic: Money, Credit, Globalisation and Consumer Rights
questions.q: Why do banks usually ask for collateral before giving a loan?
options: To ensure repayment, since the bank can recover its money if the borrower fails to pay
questions.explanation: Collateral reduces the lender’s risk.

questions.topic: Money, Credit, Globalisation and Consumer Rights
questions.q: List any three rights of consumers.
questions.answer: Consumers have the right to safety, the right to be informed, the right to choose, the right to be heard, the right to seek redressal and the right to consumer education.
questions.explanation: These rights are recognised under the Consumer Protection Act.

questions.topic: Money, Credit, Globalisation and Consumer Rights
questions.q: How has information and communication technology helped globalisation?
questions.answer: Telecommunications, computers and the internet allow information to travel instantly and cheaply, so companies can coordinate production, sell services such as call centres and software from distant countries, and trade easily across borders.
keyPoints: Services and production can be located anywhere
questions.explanation: Technology has reduced distance as a barrier.

questions.q: What was the slogan of the French Revolution?
questions.explanation: ‘Liberty, Equality, Fraternity’ expressed the ideals of the French Revolution.

questions.q: In which year did Mahatma Gandhi return to India from South Africa?
questions.explanation: Gandhiji returned to India in January 1915.

questions.q: The official language of the Union of India is
questions.explanation: Hindi in Devanagari script is the official language, and English is also used for official purposes.

questions.q: The Hirakud Dam is built across which river?
questions.explanation: Hirakud, in Odisha, is built on the Mahanadi.

questions.topic: Development and the Sectors of the Economy
questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of the organised sector?
options: Job security and fixed working hours
questions.explanation: Organised-sector workers usually enjoy security, fixed hours and benefits.

questions.topic: Money, Credit, Globalisation and Consumer Rights
questions.q: Why is the rupee accepted as money in India?
options: Because it is made of gold
Because it is authorised by the government and law, and people accept it as payment
questions.explanation: Currency is accepted because of its legal authorisation and general trust.

questions.q: What are the merits of democracy compared with other forms of government?
questions.answer: Democracy makes government accountable to the people, improves the quality of decisions through discussion, provides ways of resolving conflicts peacefully and enhances equality and dignity of citizens.
questions.explanation: Democracy’s value lies in accountability and respect for citizens.

questions.q: What are the three lists of subjects in the Indian Constitution? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: The Union List includes subjects such as defence; the State List has subjects such as police and agriculture; and the Concurrent List contains subjects such as education and forests, on which both can make laws.
questions.explanation: The lists divide legislative powers between the Union and the states.
